The clinical picture of upper motor neuron signs (burning pain, paresthesias) combined with definitive lower motor neuron signs (fasciculations, absent reflexes, muscle weakness) in the hands strongly suggests a motor neuron disease rather than a peripheral neuropathy or radiculopathy.
